issues.ownership_check: Unassigned (jamadeo/jbg assignments removed). Reporter A-Sverdrup made no claim.
issues.platform_plan: Mac ARM64, CPU only: vitest for the new Desktop list entry/persistence/unavailable-state components (cd ui/desktop && npm test), Rust unit tests around explicit_model_path listing/persistence with a small dummy .gguf fixture file (no inference run needed to validate add/persist/missing-file states); manual smoke via the desktop app with a real small GGUF is optional and still CPU-capable (llama.cpp Metal/CPU).

issues.title: In-Chat annotation (quote selected conversation text into the composer)
issues.importance_rationale: UX convenience: users cannot easily quote a portion of the chat to discuss it; no data loss or breakage, but a frequently-used interaction in comparable chat UIs.
issues.ownership_check: Unassigned (jbg assignment removed). Reporter SyncNovate made no claim.
issues.platform_plan: Mac ARM64, CPU only: implement in ui/desktop React components; vitest unit tests for the selection-action (multiline, existing-draft preservation, code-block quoting per jbg's verification list); manual check via the desktop dev app. No backend, no GPU, no credentials.

issues.title: Define nonterminal input ownership for interactive elicitation
issues.importance_rationale: Edge-case input-routing correctness: queued nonterminal stdin intended as conversation input can be silently consumed by extension elicitation forms in CLI automation; low frequency but confusing when hit, and the maintainer has settled the desired behavior.
issues.ownership_check: Unassigned (jamadeo assignment removed). Author jbg; no claim comments.
issues.platform_plan: Mac ARM64, CPU only: cargo test -p goose-cli with unit tests around the elicitation input dispatch (non-terminal stdin => explicit error instead of consuming queued input; terminal path unchanged); manual check by piping stdin to 'goose run --interactive --text ...' with an extension form fixture. Both agent-loop paths per the issue's verification list.

issues.title: Add supported backends attribute to stages
issues.importance_rationale: Stages that only work on one backend (notably deduplication on RayActorPool) currently run on incompatible executors and produce unexpected behavior or errors with no guardrail - a silent-wrong-results / confusing-failure class for pipeline users.
issues.ownership_check: Unassigned; 0 comments; no claim of any age; no maintainer plan comment. Filed by the team (2025-09-30) as an acknowledged gap - deep backlog is explicitly acceptable per the repo's small-fix on-ramp.
issues.platform_plan: Mac ARM64 / Linux CPU container, pure CPU: uv/pip install the text-cpu extra; add supported_backends (default: all three) to ProcessingStage, executor-side validation raising a clear error, and mark actor-pool-only dedup stages; pytest tests/ for the attribute, the validation error path, and no-regression on existing CPU stage tests. No GPU/RAPIDS needed for the attribute+validation mechanism.

issues.title: [Bug]: Docker conversation runtime creates linked worktree across incompatible host/container filesystem namespaces
issues.importance_rationale: priority:high by maintainers: with OH_CONVERSATION_RUNTIME=docker + worktree=true, the created worktree is immediately 'prunable' from the host - routine host-side git gc/worktree prune severs the conversation's working tree, risking loss of in-progress agent work and breaking the worktree feature for every docker-runtime user.
issues.ownership_check: Unassigned; ready-for-dev label applied by the readiness bot; only comment is the reporter's re-reproduction; no claim, no maintainer plan.
issues.platform_plan: Mac ARM64, CPU only: unit-test the worktree path/gitdir portability logic (pytest openhands-agent-server tests) with plain git - e.g. relative gitdir links or locating the worktree under the shared bind-mounted namespace - then end-to-end with Docker Desktop (CPU): run agent-server with OH_CONVERSATION_RUNTIME=docker against a host repo, create a conversation with worktree=true, assert 'git worktree list' on the host shows a valid (non-prunable) worktree. No GPU, no credentials.

issues.title: [Bug]: Docker conversation runtime cannot resolve configured title LLM profile because per-runtime profile store is empty
issues.importance_rationale: A configured title_llm_profile is silently ignored under the Docker conversation runtime (falls back to the agent LLM / truncation): user configuration does not take effect and the only signal is a server-side warning.
issues.ownership_check: Unassigned; ready-for-dev; no comments beyond the readiness bot; no claim, no maintainer plan.
issues.platform_plan: Mac ARM64, CPU only: pytest unit test that docker provisioning materializes (or proxies) the referenced LLM profile for the inner store - the profile store and provisioning env assembly are plain Python and testable without containers; e2e confirmation with Docker Desktop (CPU) by configuring title_llm_profile and asserting the inner server resolves it. No GPU; LLM call itself can be mocked.

issues.title: fix(workspace): link attached conversations in automation callbacks
issues.importance_rationale: Automations that resume a stable conversation complete with automation_runs.conversation_id empty, making runs hard to trace in Agent Canvas - a traceability gap, no data loss.
issues.ownership_check: Unassigned; ready-for-dev; filed by maintainer neubig as a spec'd small fix with acceptance criteria (including 'A failed attach does not register'); no claim comments.
issues.platform_plan: Mac ARM64, CPU only: pure pytest with a mocked workspace client following the existing RemoteConversation test patterns - assert attach() registers the ID on success and does not register on HTTP failure, and that the completion callback carries the attached ID; uv run pytest openhands-sdk tests. No Docker, no credentials.
